common_name: White Shooting Star (White-Flowered Eastern Shooting Star)

planting.note: Set out divisions or container plants in fall into moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial to full shade, marking the spot so the dormant corm isn't disturbed over summer.

directions: This naturally occurring white-flowered form of eastern shooting star lacks the pink-to-magenta pigment of the typical species, producing umbels of pure white, swept-back petals around a bright yellow anther cone. Grow it exactly as you would the species: moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, ideally alongside pink-flowered populations for color contrast in a native woodland border. Flowers are buzz-pollinated by bumblebees and are followed by a full spring-ephemeral dormancy, with foliage vanishing by early summer, so interplant with later-emerging ferns or hostas to hold the space. Division of established clumps in fall is far faster than raising plants from seed, which can take two to three years to first flower and does not always come true to the white form.
